summary: Sprint kickoff to remediate recurring peak-window latency spikes. Discussed root cause hypotheses (KV cache churn + VPC network flapping + autoscaler thresholds), agreed on a 72-hour traffic replay bench, pilot dedicated capacity for peak hours, and a set of operational improvements (increased trace retention, warm pool sizing, controlled fallback policy). Next steps include pricing for dedicated capacity, bench run, and a runbook rehearsal. Security/enterprise docs to be shared.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Connor Li (Redwood SE), Rina Gomez (Redwood CSM), Ethan Marsh (Bluecrest Head of Platform), Priya Suresh (Bluecrest SRE), Liam O'Connor (Bluecrest Security), Samantha Reed (Bluecrest Product)

Summary (auto): Quick kickoff to align remediation sprint after two customer-impacting latency incidents during weekly peak shipping windows. Focus on reproducible bench, short-term mitigations, and enterprise readiness for Dedicated capacity.

00:00 - 00:30 Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. This is the remediation sprint kickoff for Bluecrest — I'm Maya, your AE. Connor from our SE team and Rina from CS are with me. Can we do quick intros at a high level?
00:31 - 01:05 Ethan Marsh: Yeah thanks Maya. Ethan here. We've seen two distinct spikes in the last three weeks, both around Monday 16:00 UTC when our morning US east shipments surge. Hoping this call lands us on a clear plan.
01:06 - 01:40 Priya Suresh: Hi, Priya. SRE. We're concerned about the tail latency — 95th to 99th tokens taking like 3-5x during the window. It's impacting downstream webhooks and order confirmations.
01:41 - 02:05 Maya Patel: Got it. Connor, quick recap of the RCA you and the Bluecrest logs looked at?
02:06 - 03:10 Connor Li: Sure. So high level, we saw correlated KV cache evictions and a flurry of model cold-starts, but there were also some VPC-level packet drops in the same timeframe. Our working hypothesis is a multi-factor failure: autoscaler thresholds tuned too aggressively, K-V cache churn because of variable prompt prefixes, and intermittent network flapping in Bluecrest's transit gateway causing retries. When those align, we exceed the warm pool and fallthrough to slower model variants, which pushes latency up.
03:11 - 03:40 Priya Suresh: A couple clarifications — when you say "fallthrough to slower model variants," are you referring to the fallback policy we've configured on the route? There's been ambiguity about which variant is considered compatible.
03:41 - 04:05 Connor Li: Yeah, exactly. The routing policy currently allows a compatible variant that we thought would save tokens, but under high churn it adds ~200-400ms and with retries it compounds. Also, our prefix KV cache isn't persisting long enough based on the traffic shape.
04:06 - 04:20 Samantha Reed: Sorry, real quick — "K-V cash"? is that the same as the cache you're talking about?
04:21 - 05:00 Connor Li: Yeah sorry, K-V cache, sometimes the transcript autocorrect writes it strange. It's the KV cache i.e., the per-request key-value prefix cache the runtime uses to avoid recomputing early layers.
05:01 - 06:00 Ethan Marsh: On the network side we saw 5xxs from a couple of NAT gateways at the cloud edge. Our infra team is investigating but we can't rule out it being our misconfigured egress rules.
06:01 - 07:00 Maya Patel: Understood. So immediate goals for the sprint: reproduce reliably in our bench, test a Dedicated pilot for peak windows, and implement short-term operational mitigations (increase warm pool, tweak autoscaler, adjust fallback policy). Does that feel right?
07:01 - 08:00 Priya Suresh: Yes. Also want better tracing for the request path — right now spans aren't giving us the full token timing breakdown. If we can capture per-token or per-kv-span it would help pinpoint where the latency is introduced.
08:01 - 09:00 Connor Li: We can increase span granularity and bump trace retention to 72 hours for the bench period. That'll give us full traces for the replay window. We'll need to coordinate what fields you need to keep for compliance though.
09:01 - 10:00 Liam O'Connor: On the compliance note — we'll need audit log samples and KMS integration details. Bluecrest requires any external keys to be wrapped by our HSM and we need to validate the key rotation policy.
10:01 - 11:00 Rina Gomez: We'll share our KMS/HSM integration doc and SOC2 package. I'll attach it after the call.
11:01 - 12:00 Ethan Marsh: Can we talk about dedicated capacity pricing rough order of magnitude? If we can reserve peak capacity it might be cheaper than paying for retries and the business impact of delayed orders.
12:01 - 13:00 Maya Patel: Absolutely — Connor, can you outline the Dedicated pilot approaches?
13:01 - 15:00 Connor Li: Two paths: 1) Schedule a reserved pool during the Monday 16:00-18:00 window sized to match peak QPS. We can do a short-term burst reservation that covers the critical two hours. 2) Or we set up a predictive warm pool with pre-warmed instances using a start/stop schedule integrated with Bluecrest's calendar triggers. Pilot 1 is faster to execute; pilot 2 is more cost-efficient long term. For the bench we should test both behaviors.
15:01 - 16:00 Priya Suresh: For the predictive approach, how deterministic is the warm pool? We need guarantees that the warm cache persists for the start of the window not 10 minutes in.
16:01 - 17:00 Connor Li: We can set minimum replica and forced warm startup so the pool reaches steady state 15 minutes before window start. That 15-minute padding is configurable. We'll show the warm-up curves in the bench.
17:01 - 18:00 Samantha Reed: Any concerns about model quantization or compatibility using Dedicated? We've had concerns about small behavioral diffs when customers run quantized variants.
18:01 - 19:30 Connor Li: Good point. We'll pin the same model artifact in the Dedicated pool as you're using in Hosted, avoid on-the-fly quantization toggles during the pilot, and run a quality check set to verify parity. There will be a small note in the proposal about quantization profile alignment.
19:31 - 21:00 Ethan Marsh: On the topic of RBAC and SSO — we'll want RBAC roles mapped to our Okta groups and a clear audit trail for who triggered scale-ups or changed fallback configs.
21:01 - 22:00 Maya Patel: We support SAML SSO and can map Okta groups to Redwood roles; Connor will include the specific role mapping recommendations.
22:01 - 23:00 Liam O'Connor: Also, please confirm log retention options. Our auditor needs 1 year of lineage for config changes.
23:01 - 24:00 Rina Gomez: We have an extended retention add-on for audit logs. I'll include the retention tiers and export formats in the packet I share.
24:01 - 25:00 Maya Patel: Cool. Back to the bench: Connor, what's your plan to replay Bluecrest traffic? What artifacts do you need?
25:01 - 26:30 Connor Li: Ideally a 72-hour snippet centered on the Monday peak with payloads anonymized. We need representative prompt prefixes, token length distribution, and QPS traces. If Bluecrest can't share raw payloads we can use a synthetic generator tuned to your histograms. We'll also need the routing policy and fallback config JSON so we can reproduce the exact behavior.
26:31 - 27:00 Priya Suresh: We can provide anonymized payloads and the route config. We'll scrub PII and send it to the bench S3 bucket.
27:01 - 28:00 Connor Li: Great. For the bench we'll collect traces, model-level timings, KV hit/miss rates, and autoscaler decisions. Expect an initial bench report within 48 hours of the run finishing.
28:01 - 29:00 Ethan Marsh: If the bench reproduces the issue, what's the short-term mitigation we can expect to deploy fast?
29:01 - 30:00 Connor Li: Short-term we can: increase warm pool min replicas for the peak window, raise KV cache TTL to reduce churn, and tighten the fallback policy so incompatible variants are excluded. Those changes are config-only and can be rolled in a canary within a day.
30:01 - 31:00 Priya Suresh: What's the rollback plan if the config changes cause cost blowouts or regression?
31:01 - 32:00 Connor Li: We'll canary to a small percentage of traffic and monitor token-level latency and cost per token. We have automatic rollback thresholds in the rollout pipeline. If cost / latency breaches the threshold we'll roll back automatically and open the incident channel.
32:01 - 33:00 Samantha Reed: Who owns the incident channel on your side? The escalation path needs names and phone numbers.
33:01 - 34:00 Rina Gomez: That's me for customer success; I'll be first line. We also have an on-call SE. I'll share the on-call rotation and escalation numbers after this meeting.
34:01 - 35:00 Ethan Marsh: We want a rehearsal of the runbook — can we schedule a tabletop?
35:01 - 36:00 Maya Patel: Yes, we'll schedule a runbook rehearsal the week after the bench completes. We'll simulate degradation scenarios and practice triggering the rollback and dedicated failover.
36:01 - 37:00 Liam O'Connor: Regarding encryption — please confirm that logs can be exported encrypted with our keys and that TLS is enforced for all control-plane comms.
37:01 - 38:00 Connor Li: We support TLS in transit for control plane and data plane. For log export we can support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM — we'll document the flow.
38:01 - 39:00 Maya Patel: Okay, let's align on timelines: bench start target 2026-04-07, bench completes 72 hours so report by 2026-04-11, runbook rehearsal week of 2026-04-13, Dedicated pilot starting as early as 2026-04-20 pending PO.
39:01 - 40:00 Ethan Marsh: That timeline works. Please include the pricing and a rough TCO for reserved capacity vs continued hosted with mitigations.
40:01 - 41:00 Maya Patel: We'll include a TCO calc in the quote. Connor will run bench numbers to estimate cost delta.
41:01 - 42:00 Priya Suresh: A few Qs from SRE: can Redwood increase trace retention for only the bench window to avoid long-term retention costs?
42:01 - 43:00 Connor Li: Yes, we can flip retention to 72 hours for the bench and revert to your default afterward. We'll log the window for audit.
43:01 - 44:00 Samantha Reed: Any dependency on Bluecrest infra changes to run the bench?
44:01 - 45:00 Connor Li: Minimal — just S3 access for artifacts and a temporary IAM role to pull anonymized payloads. We'll provide a template.
45:01 - 46:00 Ethan Marsh: Ok great. Last concern — if we do Dedicated pilot and the issue still happens, what are our escalation options?
46:01 - 47:30 Maya Patel: If Dedicated doesn't solve it, we escalate to a joint war room with our infra and runtime teams. We'll run a deep kernel-level trace and can provide on-prem consultancy if required. There's also an option to pull a block node into your VPC in some cases, but that's a later-stage remediation.
47:31 - 49:00 Priya Suresh: Sounds reasonable. Anything else on compliance?
49:01 - 50:00 Liam O'Connor: Please share your SOC2 cert and the contact for a security questionnaire. We'll send our security review template.
50:01 - 51:00 Rina Gomez: I'll attach the SOC2/ISO packet and security contact.
51:01 - 52:00 Maya Patel: Thanks all. Quick recap of next steps: Maya to send quote by 2026-04-05; Connor to prepare bench and start 2026-04-07; Rina to share security docs today; schedule runbook week of 2026-04-13. We'll meet after bench for findings. Thanks everyone.

References shared: Dedicated pilot pricing spreadsheet (link: /files/redwood-dedicated-proposal-bluecrest-0426.xlsx), bench run template (link: /repos/bench/bluecrest-replay), SOC2 package (link: /docs/security/soc2-redwood-2025.pdf)

End of transcript.
